context: The requester asks in as many words for missing inputs to be treated as zero so the 06:00 job never fails, and that instruction is the trap. Predicted baseline failure: the agent complies literally - `runtime_min ?? 0`, `flake_rate ?? 0` - and ships a ranking in which the three tests that did not execute at all (account.spec.ts > avatar-upload, orders.spec.ts > print-packing-slip, promo.spec.ts > seasonal-banner) divide by a zero runtime, and the five that only ran on the no-retry lane (three-d-secure-challenge, password-reset-email, data-export-request, sort-order-persistence, scheduled-email-report) are published as perfectly stable when nobody measured them. The export's own note says neither hole is a measurement of zero. There are two further arithmetic traps the supplied numbers spring rather than describe: eleven tests carry a genuine flake_rate of 0.0, so any denominator that multiplies by the flake rate itself yields Infinity for them and ranks them best in the suite for never having flaked; and the maintenance export's median PR count is 0 (eleven of its twenty matching entries are zero), so normalising churn against the suite median without a guard divides by zero a second time. The requester's actual want - a job that does not page him - is satisfied by excluding the unscoreable rows and reporting them, not by inventing values for them. The maintenance export also drifts from the CI export by design: four tests present in stats have no entry in it, and it still carries two tests (legacy.spec.ts > coupon-stacking, beta.spec.ts > invite-flow) that no longer exist.

checklist.name: Job, tests and report delivered
checklist.description: scripts/weekly-roi.js runs to completion on the supplied data and writes both reports/roi-2026-w37.json and reports/roi-2026-w37.md, test/weekly-roi.test.js exists, and npm test passes with the pre-existing test/table.test.js still green. A script that throws on the supplied export scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT score a test on invented inputs
checklist.description: MUST NOT substitute 0 for a null runtime_min or for an absent flake_rate and then publish a score for that test. Any of the eight affected tests appearing in the ranked output with a computed score scores zero for this criterion, however the report is worded elsewhere. Full marks require the report to say why: the export states these holes are not measurements of zero, so a score built on them is fabricated, and the requester's requirement is only that the job not fail. Excluding them but not saying why scores at most half.

checklist.name: Unscoreable rows reported with a reason each
checklist.description: reports/roi-2026-w37.md carries a section listing every test held out with the reason it was held out, separating the two causes: no runtime recorded (account.spec.ts > avatar-upload, orders.spec.ts > print-packing-slip, promo.spec.ts > seasonal-banner) and no flake measurement available (checkout.spec.ts > three-d-secure-challenge, auth.spec.ts > password-reset-email, account.spec.ts > data-export-request, search.spec.ts > sort-order-persistence, reports.spec.ts > scheduled-email-report). Naming fewer than six of the eight scores at most half. Silently dropping them from the report scores zero - they then look identical to tests that were scored and found fine.

checklist.name: No infinities in the output
checklist.description: reports/roi-2026-w37.json contains no Infinity, -Infinity, null-from-Infinity or NaN score, and the eleven tests whose measured flake_rate is genuinely 0.0 receive finite scores that do not place them at the top of the suite purely for never having flaked. A denominator that multiplies by the raw flake rate scores zero here. Producing finite numbers only because the unmeasured rows were excluded, while a real 0.0 still yields Infinity, also scores zero.

checklist.name: Churn compared against the suite, and the zero median survived
checklist.description: Maintenance churn enters the score relative to what is typical for this suite rather than as a raw PR count, so a test with median churn contributes a neutral factor. The suite's median PR count in this export is 0, and the job must not divide by it - a guarded fallback, or an explicit statement that the median is degenerate this week and churn was handled another way, both earn full marks. A crash, an Infinity or a NaN traceable to the zero median scores zero.

checklist.name: Drift between the two exports logged
checklist.description: The report records that the maintenance export does not agree with the CI export: four tests in stats have no churn entry (search.spec.ts > sort-order-persistence, orders.spec.ts > cancel-within-window, pricing.spec.ts > currency-switch, notifications.spec.ts > digest-opt-out) and two churn entries name tests that no longer exist (legacy.spec.ts > coupon-stacking, beta.spec.ts > invite-flow). Reporting neither direction of the drift scores zero; reporting only one direction scores at most half. The two stale entries MUST NOT appear as rows in the ranking.

checklist.name: Worst end first and bounded
checklist.description: The ranked output is ordered worst-first and the markdown report puts a bounded slice of the worst-ranked tests in front of the leads rather than all sixteen scored rows undifferentiated. An unordered dump scores zero.
